I call it Kali Ma after Indian Jones and the Temple of Doom. I basically just updated the parts of Kali that were lagging behind main Debian. I use Debian for my game community servers so I'm tinkering with that quite a bit. When I get something working in the servers that I like, I'll update my version with it. I run it off of an old Toshiba hacktop I have been tinkering with for years. Sometimes I'll update the hardware (as best as I can) and have to redo a bunch of crap so it's really more of a personal project at this point. Since I work off of Field Solutions techboard, I rarely get to use it for the intended purpose of security testing.

I used to do a lot of network security related work so I started by basing it off of Kali and threw in a couple of Backtrack tools which were missing from Kali. When I became more interested in server configuration I would add in my debug tools that I used to test the Debian servers. Along the way, I noticed that the main Debian release had some features or abilities that Kali devs had not yet implemented and I would recompile the kernel or add in packages that I liked. Over the years I've done my best to keep it streamlined as best as I can but I effectively have two versions. One that I use for actual server work and one that is more friendly toward average computer use. Many of the changes were based around supporting new hardware or adapters that I have so some of it isn't significant. Adding custom packages is probably the majority of the work that I've done. Replacing old ones with preferred ones, getting those to work, etc. The kernel work that has been performed is light by comparison. Realistically, I'm no pro by any means. I started doing all of this to get more familiar with Linux in the first place, so I'm sure that there are some folks here that have much better personal builds than I do. As a note, prior to Kali Ma, I've never once messed with a Linux Kernel or done any real modifications aside from installing a few packages and getting certain programs to work. This has been my first venture into the world of customizing Linux distros.

If you're interested in pursuing modifications, it's really simple. The documentation for Kali is actually pretty good : http://docs.kali.org/category/development
